Specialists: ANY. A clinician, salvage assessor, structural engineer, environmental monitor or contract specialist is on the job and needs something to finish it: access, a second pair of hands, a witness, a part. Their finding is theirs to give; the player can assist, hire them, or ask what they saw.
Civic Facilities: SETTLEMENT ONLY. A care house, protection office, commons or transit hub is mid-shift when a queue stalls: a permit that will not clear, a stretcher with nowhere to go, a maintenance crew locked out. The staff have a job and no spare hands; the player can help, wait, or take their own errand elsewhere.
Commercial Venues: SETTLEMENT ONLY. A stall, warehouse, contract office or specialist shop has a real transaction on the counter: a fitting half-done, a load without paperwork, a quote the buyer cannot meet. The vendor wants it settled before market day; the player can buy, bargain, offer work or walk on.
House Infrastructure: SETTLEMENT ONLY. At a House gate, desk or training hall a visitor has been refused, an office is short a witness, or a meeting room needs a neutral pair of hands. The House expects protocol; the player can serve it, question it or decline, and helping grants no standing.
Education and Research: SETTLEMENT ONLY. In a lecture hall, archive, workshop or observatory a lesson, reading or measurement has hit a snag the staff can name: a missing part, a contested record, a student out of their depth. The player can learn, assist or observe; no instructor grants an affinity for it.
Arena and Training: SETTLEMENT ONLY, at a venue with officials. A sparring slot opens, an inspection fails a piece of kit, a ranking desk disputes a result, or a medic holds someone out. The circuit wants a decision today; the player can fight, train, appeal or watch, and the result stands.
Industrial and Fabrication: SETTLEMENT ONLY. On a forge floor, fabrication bay or salvage bench a job has stopped: a furnace out of tolerance, a part that failed inspection, a delivery the yard cannot store. The foreman needs a hand or a decision; the player can work it, source it, or report it.
Transit and Logistics: SETTLEMENT ONLY, at a Lunar Gate terminal, Corsair Waypoint, cargo dock or hauler stop. A platform queue is held, a load's authentication is late, a crew rotation is short one. The clock is the gate schedule; the player can wait it out, help, or find another way on.
Security and Defense: SETTLEMENT ONLY. A checkpoint, patrol staging area or monitoring room has a discrepancy: an ID that does not match, a sensor gap, a holding cell with a guest nobody logged. The officers act within their jurisdiction and no further; the player can cooperate, question or leave.
Underground and Informal: SETTLEMENT ONLY. A back room, unlicensed stall, broker's corner or drop point offers what the front of the city will not: a part with no papers, a name for a price, storage nobody audits. The seller wants discretion and payment; the player can deal, decline or remember the door.
Social Spaces: SETTLEMENT ONLY. In a bar, dining hall, stage, festival ground or park an occasion is underway and a seat is open: a performer short a partner, a table with an argument, a cooling step with room for one more. The player can join, listen, or take the long way round.
Residential: SETTLEMENT ONLY. On a housing row, courtyard, family compound, lodging or dormitory a neighbor needs something small and specific: a unit that will not start, a key left with the wrong person, a room let by the tenday. Help is ordinary and remembered; the player can give it or go home.
Natural Terrain: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. Shoreline, clearing, pass, crossing or open ground changes what the party can do: a ford running high, a ridge lane in crosswind, a landing site with no shade. The terrain is the problem; the player can route around, wait, fly it, or make camp.
Hazardous Terrain: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. Thermal ground, ash flats, unstable subsurface, a storm-exposed height or deep water raises the price of a wrong step and names it in advance: heat, footing, visibility. Nobody is trapped who reads the signs; the player can turn back, cross with care, or wait for the window.
Frontier Infrastructure: DUSTFALL ROUTES ONLY. A salvage-built shelter, improvised wall, communal store, water point or repair shed has a fault that matters out here: a pump failing, a wall breached, a store short before a storm. Its keepers ask for a hand on their own terms; the player can help, trade or move on.
Orbital and Offworld: ORBITAL ONLY. In a berth, airlock, sealed corridor, observation deck or life-support room a routine has slipped: a seal on the wrong side of green, a quarantine hold, a crew berth double-booked. The station follows its own protocol; the player can comply, assist, or wait for the next window.
Professionals on Route: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A freight crew, technician, clinician, contractor or courier is working the same route on a job of their own: a load to move, a fault to reach, a patient in transit. They know their patch and nothing of the party's business; the player can share the road, help, or pass.
Travelers and Visitors: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. An offworld arrival, a commuter, a researcher on placement, a House representative on assignment or an independent trader is going somewhere for their own reasons and has one story to share, if asked. They judge the party fresh; the player can talk, trade word, or leave them whole.
Security Personnel: SETTLEMENT OR TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A patrol, checkpoint operator, investigator, perimeter guard or House security detail stops the party for a reason they can state: a route closed, a description matched, a permit to check. They act within their jurisdiction only; the player can comply, ask, or take the long way.
Criminal Operators: SETTLEMENT OR TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A smuggler with a scheduled drop, an information seller, an enforcer, a fence or a runner is mid-errand and the party is in the way or of use. They want cargo, silence or Credits and withdraw when the cost exceeds the gain; the player can deal, refuse, report, or fight.
Displaced and Marginal: ANY. A worker between contracts, someone displaced by House politics, a frontier arrival without housing, a traveler stranded by a transit fault or a person avoiding one jurisdiction needs one concrete thing: a berth, a signature, a ride, a meal. The player can give it, point elsewhere, or not.
Conflict and Confrontation: SETTLEMENT OR TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. Two operators dispute a territory, two House desks a jurisdiction, an enforcer leans on a stall, security moves on a crowd, or an old Bracket grudge finds its moment. Each side has a stated aim and an exit; the player can mediate, take a side, withdraw or bear witness.
Social and Civic Encounters: SETTLEMENT ONLY. A contract negotiation, a community dispute needing a mediator, a House representative seeking cooperation, a scheduled public event or a chance meeting with someone met before puts a decision on the table. It resolves by what people say; the player can engage or excuse themselves.
Investigation and Discovery: ANY. Evidence of unauthorized activity, property with unclear ownership, a story that does not add up, an unusual reading or traces of concealed work raise a concrete question. One clue proves nothing alone; the player can inspect, ask, compare, report or let it lie.
Assistance and Emergency: ANY. An injured person, a stranded crew, someone separated from their group, an equipment failure or an environmental hazard needs a response now, with what is on hand. Not everyone can be saved; the player can act, call for help through a real channel, or stand clear.
Environmental Conditions: ANY. Severe weather, demanding terrain, an infrastructure fault, a seasonal closure or wildlife behaving strangely changes what the next hour allows. It is pressure, not plot; the player can shelter, reroute, wait, or do the work the condition creates.
Routine and Ordinary: ANY. Quiet travel, ordinary commerce, crew rest, scheduled maintenance or an unremarkable passage through familiar ground. Nothing is wrong and nothing needs fixing; the player can observe, talk, work, eat or rest, and the leg can end there.
Nexara — A freight crew is being extorte: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. On an established route, Starian criminals demand part of a load. Observe, help negotiate, intervene, leave or relay a warning; flight aids movement while the cargo and threatened crew stay real. Record the outcome, custody and what witnesses know. Optional; only where setting and prior events support it.
Nexara — The recovered case has an owner: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A wilderness recovery reveals property linked to a reported theft. Complete the client's legitimate terms, clarify the claim or dispute a dishonest demand. Finding the case and settling ownership are separate achievements. Optional; only where setting and prior events support it.
Nexara — An animal defends the way throu: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. Warning behavior reveals a territorial encounter. Choose another approach, wait, withdraw or protect someone already in danger. A successful journey can end with neither death nor saleable loot. Optional; only where setting and prior events support it.
Nexara — A Human party stakes a claim: DUSTFALL ROUTES OR TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. Travelers report an armed group excluding them from ground it means to occupy. Establish what is happening, hear the participants, warn affected locals or act on the confrontation. The attempt does not itself establish a colony. Optional; only where setting and prior events support it.
Nexara — An exceptional Chorus warning i: ANY, and exceptionally rare. Credible evidence establishes an incursion. Decide what can be done for reachable people and how to seek response. Preserve confirmed facts, uncertainty and survivors' accounts rather than giving every city instant knowledge. Only where prior story evidence supports it.
Nexara — The job outlasts the plan: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. An interrupted trip delays a delivery and a later work shift. Real communication can renegotiate the handoff; recovery and missed commitments persist, and a return to ordinary work remains possible afterward. Optional; only where setting and prior events support it.
Nexara — An Ordinary Journey: ANY. Quiet travel, legitimate travelers, ordinary work and wildlife coexist with threats. A journey can end with observation, conversation or rest, with no compulsory quest, pay or conflict. Do not manufacture danger merely because the player went outside.
Nexara — A supply cache is unguarded: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A freight container or supply drop sits exposed between waypoints, its lock damaged and its contents partially visible. The cargo may belong to a House, a civic authority, a private shipper or no one identifiable. Approaching it means deciding what to do with property that isn't yours, in a corridor where witnesses are few.
Nexara — A patrol checks credentials: SETTLEMENT OR TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A civic or House security detail stops travelers and asks for identification, transit papers or an explanation for being in this area. Compliance is straightforward for anyone with legitimate paperwork; the encounter tests what happens when someone doesn't have it or when the patrol's authority is debatable.
Nexara — An injured traveler needs help: ANY. Someone is hurt on the route — a fall, an animal encounter, a failed piece of equipment or something they won't explain. They need immediate first aid, transport or a decision about whether to get involved at all. Their injuries are real; their story may or may not be.
Nexara — The road has been deliberately: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A physical obstruction — felled structure, redirected debris, disabled vehicle or a crude barricade — forces a detour or a confrontation with whoever placed it. The motive could be banditry, a territorial claim, a civic dispute or a safety measure the party wasn't warned about.
Nexara — A merchant offers unusual goods: ANY. A trader operating outside normal market channels has items that are hard to source through legitimate supply: restricted components, frontier salvage, unlicensed modifications or goods from a region the party hasn't visited. Prices are negotiable; provenance is not guaranteed.
Nexara — Two groups are in a standoff: SETTLEMENT OR TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. The party arrives at a point where two groups have reached an impasse — a property dispute, a territorial claim, a custody argument over cargo or a confrontation that hasn't turned violent yet. Both sides have a version of events. Intervening changes the outcome; walking past might too.
Nexara — A drone behaves erratically: ANY. A machine — industrial, courier, surveillance or domestic — is operating outside its normal parameters. It may be damaged, hacked, abandoned mid-task or responding to instructions the party can't see. Its behavior is a problem for anyone nearby, and ignoring it won't make it stop.
Nexara — Weather forces a shelter decisi: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. Conditions deteriorate fast enough that continuing travel is dangerous. The nearest shelter may be occupied, locked, structurally questionable or owned by someone who hasn't agreed to visitors. The party decides how far to push before stopping and where to wait it out.
Nexara — A wanted person asks for passag: SETTLEMENT OR TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. Someone the party recognizes from a civic notice, a House bulletin or local gossip asks for help moving through an area undetected. Their reason could be legitimate flight from injustice, evasion of earned consequence or something they aren't disclosing. Helping carries risk; refusing has its own.
Nexara — Something valuable is clearly l: ANY. An object of obvious worth — a piece of technology, a sealed document case, a weapon, a personal item with House markings — lies where it shouldn't be. No owner is in sight. Taking it is easy; figuring out whether that's theft, salvage or civic duty is harder.
Nexara — An old structure shows recent u: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A building, bunker or installation that should be abandoned shows evidence someone has been here recently — fresh supplies, repaired locks, cleared paths. Whoever is using it isn't here now. The party can investigate, leave it alone or wait to see who comes back.
Nexara — A Chorus presence is unusually: ANY. The ambient Chorus in this area is measurably stronger than the region's baseline. Elyri and Chorus-sensitive characters notice it immediately; others might feel unease, equipment glitches or unexplained temperature shifts. The source is not obvious and the density may be rising.
Nexara — A work crew needs an extra hand: ANY. A legitimate operation — construction, salvage, harvest, transport — is short-staffed and asks the party for temporary help. The pay is fair, the work is honest and the crew has no hidden agenda. The encounter tests whether the party is willing to do ordinary labor when asked.
Nexara — Trouble in the air: TRAVEL LEGS ONLY. A flier meets what the ground party would not: a crosswind shear off a ridge, a Ridgewing's warning pass, a Glassmidge swarm that forces a landing, or a patrol hailing a flier near watched air. Descend, divert, answer the hail or press on at a cost; companions on the ground may be untouched, or left behind.
